newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala's Menchu criticizes amnesty seekers.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's Menchu criticizes amnesty seekers.

text.p: Guatemalan Nobel laureate Rigoberta Menchu has sharply criticised four high-ranking army officers for seeking amnesty for the 1990 murder of sociologist Myrna Mack.

A general, three colonels and 10 members of a paramilitary patrol managed by the army -- all accused of murder -- applied for amnesty on Monday under a new law that was part of a recent peace pact between the government and leftist rebels.
"We energetically condemn the way some people are trying to twist the spirit of the peace process and the laws that came out of that process," Menchu told reporters at a news conference.

The government and rebels signed the treaty on December 29, ending 35 years of civil war and putting into effect a limited amnesty, approved by Congress, for political crimes and common crimes linked to the war. Murder, assassination or massacre were not covered under the law.
The general and the three colonels were accused of ordering a soldier to murder Mack because of her work on the displacement of the nation's Indians during the war.
